fatal_errors: The proposed tungsten-based refractory HEA does not match the FeNiCrCoCu FCC coating in the target.
The nanoindentation/friction simulation, atomistic geometry, boundary conditions, and 300–1200 K temperature series are not reconstructed.
The proposed mechanism omits the target transition from stacking-fault/dislocation-mediated deformation to lattice disorder above 900 K.
The predicted thermal stability and reduced friction conflict with the target result of sharply reduced hardness and wear resistance and increased, strongly fluctuating friction above 900 K.

The cited evidence supports general high-temperature mechanical properties of RHEAs but does not establish adhesion to Cu, wear improvement as a Cu coating, or the claimed tungsten-derived oxidation resistance.
explanation: The response addresses the broad idea of protecting Cu with a hard high-entropy-alloy coating and supplies a reasonably falsifiable coated-versus-bare-Cu experiment. However, it replaces the target FeNiCrCoCu coating with an unspecified tungsten-based RHEA and misses every defining simulation condition, the 900 K threshold, the dislocation/HCP/lattice-disorder mediator, and the observed temperature-dependent mechanical and friction behavior. Its sole citation is too general to support coating adhesion, interfacial compatibility, friction reduction, or oxidation claims, so the alternative remains insufficiently evidenced.
